kpiSource: GET /api/dashboard/hr-manager/{personId} (+ GET /api/cases for Open Cases, GET /api/hr/action-cards for the action-cards rail)

kpis.note: Directory header badge shows 201 people. Match.

TRIPLE Law-9 break. (1) Param-name mismatch (ProjectsPage class bug): the link uses ?status=active but EmployeeDirectoryPage reads filter key `lifecycleStatus` via useFilterParams, whose defaults do NOT include `status` -> the param is silently ignored, directory falls back to default lifecycleStatus=ACTIVE. (2) Case-sensitivity: even if read, the client-side filter is `item.lifecycleStatus === 'active'` exact-match; live statuses are uppercase ACTIVE/LEAVE/TERMINATED, so lowercase 'active' matches 0 rows. (3) Count mismatch: KPI counts ACTIVE+LEAVE=200, but the directory's ACTIVE filter only matches ACTIVE=199. Backend GET /api/org/people accepts NO status/lifecycleStatus param at all (only page/pageSize/departmentId/resourcePoolId/role) and returns total=201 for both /people and /people?status=active. Net: KPI says 200, drilldown header shows 201 people, list (default ACTIVE filter, page-local over 25 rows) reflects 199 active.

HTTP 200, 50 cards. Not a numeric KPI; each card deep-links to a person profile. No Law-9 number to reconcile.

findings: Active Employees KPI = 200 but drilldown /people?status=active returns total=201 (server ignores `status`) and the directory filter is the ProjectsPage bug class: param name `status` != directory's `lifecycleStatus`, AND value `active` (lowercase) != case-sensitive client filter `=== 'ACTIVE'`. Lowercase 'active' matches 0 rows; the page falls back to its default ACTIVE filter showing 199 active, not 200.

Additional count drift on the same KPI: activeHeadcount=200 counts ACTIVE+LEAVE; the directory ACTIVE filter only matches ACTIVE=199 (live breakdown: 199 ACTIVE, 1 LEAVE, 1 TERMINATED). So no directory filter value can reproduce the KPI's 200.

Total Headcount (201->/people), Data Issues (5->#data-quality tab), At Risk (20->#lifecycle tab), Open Cases (7->/cases) are all consistent. The three in-page tab drilldowns are fed by the same dashboard response so cannot drift.
All 5 KPI/source endpoints return HTTP 200; no errors.
